fix: No code change; correct the inventory to add the forest out-of-bag path (tuning.py:1737, pipeline.py:540-541) and the time-to-event refusal of tuned families (pipeline.py:528-532), and cite the stronger tests (test_tuning_engine.py::test_t3_*, test_elastic_net_penalty.py::test_the_inner_curve_*) instead of the arithmetic-only one.
evidence: Both referees judged the claim true, and the code matches it: pooled_loss is sum(w*loss)/sum(w) over every inner row (tuning.py:998-1013), Loss admits only mse/log_loss/rps (tuning.py:88), and choose() takes the rounded argmin (tuning.py:1016). The only gap is the inventory's: a forest with one row per unit, no time order, the sample answer and no outcome-reading step pools its out-of-bag predictions instead, which is still a pooled strictly proper loss, so the app's real claim holds (audit's corrected statement accepted).

fix: No code change; restate the inventory as 'a box of narrowed conventions with XGBoost's defaults always a candidate' (xgboost_family.py:482-515, RECIPES §4.1), and optionally give the Dimension source strings at xgboost_family.py:484-497 a 'narrowed from' prefix so the registry does not attribute depth 2-10 or rounds 25-1,000 to Probst.
evidence: The app never says the box 'contains the well-performing settings': users see only 'Its settings are searched inside every training fold, with XGBoost's defaults always among the candidates' (xgboost_family.py:513), and RECIPES calls the ranges 'conventions, narrowed'; the per-dimension source strings feed only the citation-registry check (base.py:687-702), not user text. Referee A is right that Probst's Table 3 puts tuned depth (5.6-14) and rounds (920-4,551) partly outside the box, but rounds are searched without early stopping only below an effective size of 1,500 (tuning.py:94), where lr up to 0.3 x 1,000 rounds is ample, and Referee B's equal-budget simulation found no loss.

fix: Reword the refusal at decisions.py:4832-4836 to the regime Sisk et al. support: 'a new row can arrive with blanks and has no outcome, and when it can, Sisk et al. 2023 found leaving the outcome out of the imputation preferred'; also note that with complete data at deployment they recommend the opposite, and say 'unless the purpose is inference' rather than 'under prediction' since the check also fires when no purpose is set (decisions.py:4830).
evidence: Both referees and the audit agree that Sisk et al. 2023 recommend putting the outcome in development-data MI when deployment data are complete, and prefer leaving it out only when missingness is allowed at deployment. So citing them for an unconditional rule overstates the source. The refusal itself is defensible in the main regime: the app's MI is whole-table and outcome-inclusive, which would leak a held-out row's outcome, and the deployed pipeline must fill blanks without an outcome. In-fold outcome-inclusive MI isn't implemented, so no valid estimate is being withheld, only overstated in its scope.

fix: At percent_energy.py:62-64 say 'every value is at most 1, which reads as fractions (0.35 for 35%)' instead of 'it holds fractions', and add an exit at decisions.py:4548-4552 that confirms the values are genuine percentages.
evidence: The 0-100 bound is definitional; the max <= 1 rule is a data-sanity heuristic stated to the user as fact, as both referees say. The false-positive regime is narrow in this app: the name gate admits only protein, carbohydrate, fat (including trans and SFA/PUFA), alcohol, fiber and sugars (EPA, DHA, ALA and omega-3 names are not admitted, as I checked with is_percent_of_energy), and at the default 5-point step (decisions.py:816) a genuine column with max <= 1 has no rows on support anyway. A refusal only bites for trans fat or alcohol in a small low-intake sample with a user-reduced step.

fix: At missing.py:1764-1768, replace 'more than the 10% at which CLINICAL_SURVEY_PACK flags listwise deletion' with 'more than 10%, a convention this app uses to prompt a look; the share lost does not measure bias', and add to the sentence that kept-vs-dropped differences in predictors are expected even when complete cases are unbiased.
evidence: Both referees are right that the 10% figure is a rule of thumb (Bennett 2001) and that the share missing does not measure complete-case bias (Madley-Dowd 2019, White & Carlin 2010). But the app only warns, and its sentence already states the right condition: 'unbiased only if whether a value is missing does not depend on the outcome, given the predictors' (missing.py:1766-1767). What remains is labeling: the user-facing text cites an internal file name as the authority for an unsourced threshold.

fix: Optional wording only: at stages/effects.py:1239 say 'the test finds the hazard ratio changes over follow-up' rather than asserting it, and note beside models/survival.py:60 that the fit stage's 0.01/P is a multiplicity-adjusted screen over all columns, not the exposure's check.
evidence: Referee B is right: testing the exposure's own cox.zph term is the relevant check for the exposure's hazard ratio, and the reading already labels 0.05 as 'the customary' level (stages/effects.py:1229-1240), so the convention is labeled. Referee A's objection, that a test tracks detectability rather than size, applies to any test-based diagnostic; here the failure only offers exits (period hazard ratios, keep labeled) and refuses nothing. The fit stage's 0.01/P (survival.py:518) answers a different question, a screen over every column with multiplicity control, and its silence is never shown as a pass, so the two thresholds do not contradict each other.

fix: Change 'Monte Carlo error at most' to 'Monte Carlo standard error about' at stages/time_varying.py:1221, and rewrite the docstring at models/time_varying.py:79-81 to say it estimates the error when the base is resampled (the default, SIMULATIONS = 10,000) and overstates it only when n_sim equals the units.
evidence: My simulation used the app's own tv.gformula (GTRUTH spec, 600 units, 300 seeds). With the default resampled base (n_sim = 3,000), the reported max(sd/sqrt(n)) was 0.00156 against a true run-to-run SD of 0.00168, below it in every run. With n_sim = units it was 0.00350 against 0.00261, a true upper bound. Referee B and the audit are confirmed: in the default regime the figure is an estimate, not a bound. The error is far below the sampling error, so the impact is cosmetic.

fix: Relabel 'no clustering without a confirmed unit' in readings.py:20-24 (and BLUEPRINT §14.1) as the leash-safe path, which for held-out and cross-validated scores is the optimistic one. When an identifier repeats but did not group the folds, add the seal's 'treat as exploratory' note to the fold sentence built in stages/rows.py (~1930-1944).
evidence: Both referees are right on the statistics: splitting a unit's rows across train and test is the optimistic direction, so 'conservative' is backwards. The behavior is mostly defended by asking. A 'repeated' grain answer must name its column (sequence.py:178-184). 'One row per unit' against repeating data needs an attestation (sequence.py:200-205). Every ungrouped seal says 'treat held-out scores as exploratory', with a 'Keep each X's rows together' exit (seal.py:254-292, row_previews.py:556-572). The gap is the CV folds and inner tuning folds (split_inputs, rows.py:1947-1977): they ungroup in the same cases without saying so, and that can favor models that memorize units.

fix: In covariate_guesses.py:90-96, make the demographic reason lens-neutral ('set before the exposure', not 'before the diet was measured'). Give income, poverty ratio, occupation, marital status and SES (covariate_guesses.py:151-152) a guess of after-exposure 'unknown', or add the caveat that in cross-sectional data they can follow the exposure or the outcome. Keep age, sex and race/ethnicity as pre-exposure.
evidence: Both referees agree that income, occupation and marital status measured at the same visit can be consequences of the exposure or the outcome. The card asserts 'set before the diet was measured' as fact. The guess also applies under every lens, since adjustment_card has no lens gate (estimand.py:971-985), so a clinical exposure gets text about 'the diet'. The behavior is defensible in the main regime: adjusting for SES is the field's Models 1-2 convention, labeled as such and confirmed by the user. So this is a wording and scope fix, not a harmful default.

fix: In methods/energy.py describe_model, when no exposure or adjusted term carries energy (terms empty with a method set, energy.py:1657-1704), state 'more of the nutrient at the same total energy; it carries no energy, so nothing is substituted' instead of METHOD_TABLE's substitution estimand (energy.py:153-155, 167-171). Scope the teaching at content.py:1099-1104 and 1397-1402 to energy-bearing nutrients.
evidence: Both referees found the substitution reading wrong for a nutrient that carries no energy. I confirmed it reaches users: the energy question stays open under the dietary lens for any exposure (interview.py:278-299). describe_model for a sodium_mg exposure with the residual or standard method returns 'more of the nutrient at the same total energy, in place of the average of all other energy sources' and '...implicitly a substitution for the average of all other energy sources'. For macronutrients the reading is correct and certified by test_5b (audit accepted), so the main regime is right and only the scope is wrong.

fix: Either add a censored lever for TNTC (lower-bound value plus a censoring indicator), or make the 'Read as numbers' consequence at repairs.py:927-933 say that blanked TNTC cells are right-censored highs whose deletion biases the column downward. Also remove 'tntc' from the failure tokens and LooksFor text (clinical.py:138, packs.py:5573), and quote the BAM 15-300 colonies-per-plate range only for plate counts (finding_words.py:303-306).
